# ML Fundamentals, Transformer & Regularization

[← Snapchat](../README.md) · [Every Snapchat question](../../snapchat.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/ml-fundamentals-transformer-and-regularization)

`ml-knowledge` `optimization` `transformer`

---

## Requirements

Prepare for a spoken ML fundamentals interview that may shift rapidly among:

1. Overfitting in linear models compared with deep neural networks.
2. Bias-variance decomposition and imbalanced data.
3. L1 and L2 regularization, dropout, early stopping, augmentation, and weight decay.
4. Batch normalization versus layer normalization, including learned parameters and differences between training and inference.
5. Optimizers and objective functions.
6. Transformer components: Q/K/V, scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, residual connections, normalization, feed-forward layers, and positional encoding.
7. A project deep dive covering data, model selection, metrics, the offline-to-online gap, deployment, and failure cases.

## Notes

Answers should be brief and make clear comparisons. When discussing overfitting, distinguish linear-model methods such as feature selection and L1/L2 regularization from DNN methods such as dropout, augmentation, early stopping, weight decay, and normalization. Use the difference between training and validation loss to identify overfitting.

For attention, state the usual expression explicitly: `softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))V`. The central idea is that, without positional information, ordinary self-attention is permutation-invariant; therefore, the model requires sinusoidal, learned, rotary, or relative positional encoding to capture order.

In a project deep dive, go beyond the architecture. Describe why ML was necessary, the baseline, the metric that changed, how labels were gathered, how the model was served, and what was monitored after release.

## Preparation

- Create one-page responses covering overfitting, imbalance, normalization, optimizers, and Transformer attention.
- Rehearse a five-minute project explanation centered on the metric, data, model, experiment, and production takeaway.
- Practice compact comparisons: batch normalization versus layer normalization, L1 versus L2, SFT versus ranking-oriented objectives, and offline versus online metrics.
- Reproduce the attention equation from memory and describe the role of each term.
